definition.text: One product's velocity, growth and acceleration in one demand family on day t.
`now` and `week_ago` are its rows for t and t−7 (None: no row). `days_observed` counts the days since its first row in the family, t included, as Lifecycle reads it (DEC-307).

items: V7(t) = units over t−6..t from a covered t−7 (DEC-275 d).
G7(t) = ln((V7(t) + 5) / (V7(t−7) + 5)), both weeks over the listings covered at t−14 and t.
Acc(t) = G7(t) − G7(t−7), from the two rows' stored G7.

definition.text: The rows already apply the gap rules (DEC-275 d): a target-coverage gap over 3 days or an uncovered window end stores NULL; a shorter gap keeps the exact value and sets has_gap. A NULL here says why:

items: no source: no row at t; the family has no series for the product (DEC-040).
insufficient history: fewer days than the window needs: 8 (V7), 15 (G7), 22 (Acc).
gap <window>: history enough but NULL; the window is t-7..t, t-14..t or t-21..t-7 (G7(t−7)).

definition.text: Nothing is interpolated or carried forward: only the rows at t and t−7 are read.

definition.text: One product's stage on day t from its primary demand family's feature rows (DEC-275).

Inputs come from the rows at t and t−7: `v7` = V7(t), `v7_prev` = V7(t−7), `g7` = G7(t) and `g7_prev` = G7(t−7), so acceleration is `g7 − g7_prev`. G7 is the week-on-week growth ln((V7 + 5) / (V7 prev + 5)), so "+20%" below means G7 ≥ ln 1.2. `days_observed` is the days since the family's first row, t included, as Velocity reads it (0: no demand family). `has_gap` is either row's gap flag. `age_days` is days since the source's launch date (None: unknown).
No stage, with its reason, never a guessed one:

items: no source: no demand family, delisted or not.
insufficient history: fewer than 15 days observed, or V7(t), V7(t−7) or G7(t) missing without a gap (a stable listing set still too new).
gap: a gap flag on either row, even when every value is present. Gaps are never filled in.

definition.text: Otherwise the first rule that holds wins:

items: dead · delisted: every listing is delisted. Checked before history: a fact, not a trend.
dead · no sales: at most 1 unit in each of the last two weeks.
declining · two weeks down: growth at or below −20% this week and last week.
declining · sharp drop: growth at or below −36% this week (G7 ≤ 2 ln 0.8).
peaking · braking: growth at or above +20%, but 0.25 or more below last week's.
peaking · plateau: growth under +20%: flat, a stall after a run, or one week down that isn't a decline yet.
emerging · new and growing: growth at or above +20%, launched 28 days ago or less, and at least 3 units this week.
rising · growing: growth at or above +20% otherwise.

definition.text: Until G7(t−7) exists (a product's first 21 days) "two weeks down" and "braking" can't hold. Hysteresis (two nights before a change shows) is the nightly job's (pulso_ml.scores.nightly).

definition.text: How crowded each product already is on day t, 0–100: higher is more saturated.

`categories` holds every product to score: its category and that category's ancestors, nearest first (empty when it has none). `rows` are day t's `shp_sellers` feature rows. Each input is a robust z within the product's category, falling back up its ancestors to every product (Score Definitions §4):

items: shp_sellers: ln(1 + s), s the stores with a live listing of it, counting every tracked store: "9 stores sell this" holds whenever they were added. Required.
shp_seller_g28: ln((p_t + 1) / (p_t−28 + 1)) over the stable panel, the stores tracked since t−28 alone, so a batch of newly tracked stores never reads as growth.
ads_active: no source yet, so always missing.

definition.text: T = Σ w × z / Σ w over the present inputs: a missing one gets weight 0 and the rest renormalise (DEC-040). Saturation = clamp(50 + 50 × T / 3, 0, 100), banded low below `low_below`, high above `high_above`, medium between.
No value, with its reason, never 0:

items: no seller count: the product has no `shp_sellers` row, or one written before them.
seller counts don't vary: no category, nor the whole set, has a spread to normalise by.

definition.text: How strongly each product is trending on day t, 0–100 (Beta until a forecast is promoted).

`categories` holds every product to score: its category and that category's ancestors, nearest first (empty when it has none). `rows` are day t's feature rows, every family; `week_ago` are day t−7's. `primary` names each product's primary demand family (vault Demand Signals rule 1); `saturation` holds its Saturation Score (SC-3). Each input is a robust z within the product's category, falling back up its ancestors to every product when n < 30 or MAD = 0, winsorized to ±3 (Score Definitions §4):

items: <family>_g7: G7 = ln((V7(t) + 5) / (V7(t−7) + 5)) in the primary family, as stored: log growth, so 3 → 30 units reads 1.48, never +900%, and both weeks count only the listings covered at t−14 and t, so newly tracked listings never read as growth. Required.
<family>_acc: G7(t) − G7(t−7) in the same family, from the two days' rows.
gt_slope: ln((m4 + 1) / (m8 + 1)) within one Trends capture, as stored (R-18).
ads_growth: no source yet, so always missing.

definition.text: Each input's cohort is every product asked for with a value in it; families never mix. T = Σ w × z / Σ w over the present inputs: a missing one gets weight 0 and the rest renormalise (DEC-040). Then pre = 50 + 50 × T / 3, and Trend = clamp(pre − penalty, 0, 100) with penalty = 15 × max(0, (Saturation − 50) / 50) points. Without a Saturation the penalty is missing: nothing is taken off and `missing` names it.
No value, with its reason, never 0:

items: no demand family: the product has no primary family. Search slope alone never scores.
no velocity growth: no G7 in that family on day t (no row, or a NULL one).
velocity growth doesn't vary: no category, nor the whole set, has a spread to normalise by.

Missing with no `source` reads "no source yet"; missing with a source reads "insufficient signal" (vault Score Definitions §7). A missing input has weight_eff 0 and no contribution, so nothing downstream can show it as 0.

missing_inputs.text: Missing with no `source` reads "no source yet"; missing with a source reads "insufficient signal" (vault Score Definitions §7). A missing input has weight_eff 0 and no contribution, so nothing downstream can show it as 0.

renormalisation.text: DEC-040: a missing input gets weight 0 and the present ones rescale to sum to 1.

Returns Σ weight_eff × z over the present inputs, None when none is present (the score's value is then NULL, never 0), and the explanation. A score that maps that sum onto 0–100 linearly (Trend and Saturation: 50 + 50 × sum / 3) gets each input's points by the same factor × its contribution.

versioning.text: (model_version, digest) of a frozen config dataclass with a `revision` field.

The FEATURE_VERSION rule (pulso_ml.features.demand): `{revision:03d}-{sha256[:12]}` of the sorted-key JSON, so any config change makes a new version and versions sort by revision. Bump `revision` with any change to a score's maths.

limitations: Collection runs on the owner's PC until Railway go-live (DEC-001), so days it is off are gaps: marked on every input they touch, never filled in.
The Shopify store crawler stays off (DEC-261): no input reads Shopify stores' stock or seller counts.
